thread:
Liam: Quick sync — I uploaded the weekly regional capacity dump. Short TL;DR: EU (orca-eu1) shows a 14% shortfall vs expected headroom for peak slots, APAC (kite-apac2) is hit by intermittent egress throttles that spike latency, and US-west (heron-us-west) has higher preemptible churn than forecast. Need decisions on temporary hedges and whether to run a brief pre-warm this weekend. Link: https://redwood/intra/capacity/3216540987

Mia: Can you paste the adjusted GPU-hours projection? the spreadsheet has a bunch of tabs, hard to follow the delta from last week.

Liam: sure — pulled the cluster-summary block here. Reason we call for a 6% buffer in eu is because queue latency tails pushed expected token throughput down ~9% during Tuesday peak. Small table:
```
cluster           projected_hours  delta_vs_plan  suggested_action
orca-eu1          95,200           -14%          pre-warm +12 nodes
kite-apac2        48,700           -9%           hold routing, fix egress
heron-us-west     132,400          -4%           increase reserved mix 10%
```

Omar: @Liam re kite-apac2 — the egress throttles were traced to a misconfigured NAT gateway on the new VPC. Networking team pushed a partial fix at 09:40 UTC, but we still see 6-8 Gbps bursts that push queues. If we don't fix fully by Friday, we should route a subset of traffic to kite-apac1 until the NAT is hardened.

Jen: I can open a short-lived reserved pool in apac for 72 hours (spot vs reserved mix 60/40). Cost delta estimate: ~$7.6k for 72h to cover 12 nodes pre-warm. That buys us time to stabilize the NAT and re-run perf tests. @finance FYI — will need approval for commit.

Anya: putting a quick checklist into the runbook: update failover routing, add a telemetry alert for egress-latency > 200ms, and note which customers we should throttle if things degrade. Also adding the canary prompt set to smoke the latency-sensitive evals.

capacity-bot: Action created: CAP-3216 "APAC NAT harden + temporary reserved pool" assigned to Jen, due 2026-03-20. Board: https://redwood/boards/capacity/CAP-3216

Mia: question on the math you used for EU pre-warm: 12 nodes -> that seems like a blunt instrument. Any chance we can do fractional scaling with micro-batches to avoid full nodes?

Liam: good call. We can try staged micro-batching and prefix cache warm first — plan A: micro-batch + cache for the top 30% routes (low lift, minimal cost). Plan B: if queues don't improve within 12h, spin the 12-node pre-warm. We'll monitor token-per-second and queue-percentile.

Omar: putting the NAT harden schedule: ETA patch Friday 02:00-04:00 UTC, post-deploy smoke, then 4h observation window. If we see recurrence we failover traffic to kite-apac1 (manual).

Jen: submitted the short-term reserved request to finance. If approved, I'll spin nodes and label them apac-temp-prewarm. Will add autoscale policy to drain after 72h.

Anya: I'll update the capacity dashboard with a special "temp-reserved" tag so cost shows separately for the next billing cycle. Also adding a metric for "prewarm_util" so we can see waste.

Liam: OK — owners/next-steps: Jen = provision if finance greenlights, Omar = NAT harden deploy + smoke, Anya = dashboard+alerts, Mia = watch throughput during micro-batch test, me = coordinate rollback plan and comms to CS for impacted customers. We'll reconvene in 24h and I’ll post an updated summary. :thumbsup:
